key_insight: The paper introduces Turbo, a transformer-based reinforcement learning framework that lets microrobotic swarms navigate and avoid obstacles autonomously in previously unknown environments. Its key breakthrough is enabling simulation-to-real transfer, so policies trained in simulation can work on physical robots.
problem_solved: Autonomous control of microrobotic swarms is difficult because real-world environments are unknown, dynamic, and hard to model accurately. The paper addresses the challenge of training navigation and obstacle-avoidance policies that remain effective when transferred from simulation to physical swarms.
method: Uses a transformer-based reinforcement learning policy to model swarm behavior and decision-making.
Trains the navigation system in simulation with a focus on generalization across unfamiliar environments.
Transfers the learned policy to real microrobotic swarms for autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how modern sequence models and reinforcement learning can be combined to solve hard sim-to-real robotics problems. It is especially relevant for deploying learned policies in safety-critical, highly constrained multi-agent systems.

paper_title: Autonomous navigation of intelligent microrobotic swarms in unknown environments
paper_authors: Xuanyu An, Shengming Luo, Haoyu Zhang, Qijun Yang, Yuanbiao Ma
